The code can handle this type?
Yes, makes sense. Passing unixfd across services can get messy. We’ll switch to a file-based approach and share the path instead.
Done
Suggest changing this back?  AFAIK PDI handles this type fine.  Passing around file paths is bug prone and really should be added to anti-patterns.md.
I'm surprised to see this being considered AMD-specific.
Moved to xyz .
done
Noticed already another reveiw https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/+/78683 is in progress.

Also for your perusal in case it is useful:

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/q/topic:%22cperlog%22
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/docs/+/83766
Where is this requirement coming from?  Can we provide the rationale here for future readers?  If it MUST be bounded, we MUST have an actual bound, not a recommendation I think.
Done
Are applications other than bmcweb going to use this field?  How will they use it?  If it is just bmcweb, why not just have bmcweb do the decoding with libcper?

This field exists to provide a shared, lightweight, structured CPER view at the DBus layer, avoiding duplicated decoding logic and enabling multiple consumers beyond bmcweb. While today the primary consumer is bmcweb, defining it here allows other applications to easily leverage it in the future without introducing new dependencies or duplicate parsing logic.

The decoding logic is all in libcper so I don't think there is any duplication?

If you really need CPER fields for other application logic (although I have no idea what those would be), those could just be first class dbus properties.  If you are just passing the JSON so that a client application can forward it on, the client application could just use libcper.
above you have must...these should be consistent I think.
Done
Can more be said about this property?  Is always just the path to a CPU?  How will it be used?

Yes.
Not limited to CPU—this points to the originating component (CPU, GPU etc.) and can be used to correlate with inventory/FRU for diagnostics.

The only use I can think of for this is the OriginOfCondition property in the Redfish LogEntry, which is optional.  If I were you, I'd leave this out of the initial implementation to keep it focused and as small/simple as possible.

This is still not useful in my mind.  I can just say the upper limit on my implementation is 1GB, effectively working around the requirement.  For it to be useful, it has to be bound to a specific number for all implementations, or just drop the requirement about bounding altogether.
sure will remove.
Since this was @patrick@stwcx.xyz guidance and he is the maintainer, I suggest you don't remove until he has a chance to provide feedback.
Rephrased
Is Redfish leaking into our abstraction layer here?

Is this will help to avoid confusion ?
name: AdditionalDataObject
type: object_path
This is un-enforceable as written - there needs to be a number associated with this.

Do you think it would be helpful to include a guideline like:
"Implementations SHOULD ensure that this data remains reasonably small (e.g., a few kilobytes) to avoid large DBus payloads"?
